historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_10yr_cagr (FY2016-FY2026), a through-cycle span that brackets COVID
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All 3/5-year CAGRs are distorted by the COVID cycle: the 5-year window starts at the FY2021 trough (revenue 3,816, negative EPS and owner FCF), the 3-year window starts at the FY2023 yield supercycle (owner FCF 7,505 on deferred capex), and equity is distorted by the 2020-21 rights/MCB issuance and their FY2022-24 redemption. Equity CAGR (-4.4% 3yr) diverges >30% from revenue CAGR; it is NOT used. The 10-year revenue CAGR (~3.0%, consistent with ASK growth 154.5bn FY17 -> 182.8bn FY26) is the through-cycle anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC (interest income not in OCF). SBC is 0.1-0.2% of revenue throughout, so the owner and reported FCF CAGRs are near-identical; the decline in FCF since FY2023 is capex normalising after COVID deferrals, not SBC. Pre-COVID (FY2017-FY2020) reported FCF was negative every year during the previous fleet renewal (capex 3.9-5.6bn/yr).

scenario_narratives.base: SIA's axes are fuel versus fare pass-through, premium long-haul yield versus Gulf/LCC competition, and the fleet capex cycle. Base: the doubled jet-fuel price takes FY27 group EBITDA (pre-lease) from 24.1% to ~19% because fares lag and hedges only partly cover; margins recover to a 21.5% mid-cycle by FY29 -- below the FY23-24 yield supercycle, above pre-COVID -- as fuel normalises. Revenue grows with 3-4% capacity (ASK +3.4% in FY26) plus fare pass-through. Capex stays ~13% of revenue through the 777-9 and A350F deliveries (9.9bn committed), then ~11.5%. Air India held at its written-down book value with no further cash call.
scenario_narratives.bull: Fuel spike fades within FY27 and in-the-money hedges cushion it; competitors retrench capacity under fuel and Middle East airspace disruption, letting SIA's Changi hub and premium brand hold yields near post-COVID levels (passenger yield 11.5c vs 10.1c pre-COVID). EBITDA holds ~23.5%, revenue grows 5-7% early on network expansion (Riyadh, Madrid, Western Sydney) and Scoot's regional growth. Air India's turnaround is upside that the book-value bridge does not capture.
scenario_narratives.bear: Fuel stays elevated and drives a macro slowdown: FY27 EBITDA ~15%, FY28 revenue falls 2% as discretionary premium long-haul demand weakens (cf. FY2020 pre-COVID softness). Gulf super-connectors and Asian LCCs push yields back to pre-COVID levels; Scoot stays marginal. Mid-cycle margin settles at 19.5% while the fleet commitments keep capex at 12-13.5% of revenue, and the cash-tax deferral unwinds toward 15%. Not modelled but adjacent: an Air India recapitalisation call on SIA's 25.1%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Through-cycle owner-FCF DCF for a cyclical, capital-intensive airline: leases charged as operating cost (treatment B), cash taxes on SIA's structurally deferred basis, an FY27 fuel trough in every scenario, a 21.5% mid-cycle EBITDA margin rather than the FY23-24 peak, and a 12x cyclical terminal cap. Associates (Air India) enter at book in the bridge, outside the flows; SIAEC's minority is deducted at market.
key_risks_to_valuation: Jet fuel: fuel was 5.0bn (24.5% of revenue) in FY26; every 10% sustained move after hedging is roughly +/-2.5pp of EBITDA margin before fare pass-through
Yield normalisation toward pre-COVID levels under Gulf and Asian LCC capacity growth
Air India: further losses, a recapitalisation call on SIA's 25.1%, or another impairment (carrying value 1,134.6 after a 960.9 write-down)
Capex: 9.9bn of fleet commitments plus a 1.1bn cabin retrofit keep capex elevated regardless of the cycle
Cash-tax deferral unwinding if fleet growth slows (deferred tax liability 2,452)
Terminal value is capped at 12x terminal FCF; at an 8.5% WACC Gordon would imply more, so the cap binds and the terminal assumption is the dominant value driver

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025/26 consolidated cash flow statement, 'Share-based compensation expense' add-back 28.1 (C6L.SI_Annual_FY2026.txt:6787). No separate equity-award withholding-tax line disclosed; SGX awards are settled in treasury shares, purchases of treasury shares were 32.7 in FY26.
inputs.share_count_basis: 3,150,884,286 issued shares excluding treasury shares as at 2 June 2026 (Annual Report FY2025/26 shareholding statistics, line 11939). All S$850m 1.625% convertible bonds converted into 179.0m shares during FY26 and the mandatory convertible bonds were fully redeemed in FY2024, so no convertible dilution remains; residual RSP/PSP dilution is ~0.5% (diluted EPS 38.2c vs basic 38.4c, partly convertible-interest). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and treasury-share purchases (32.7 in FY26) fund the award settlement.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T09:06:12Z (SGX regular-session last trade, Yahoo chart API regularMarketTime)
inputs.wacc_rationale: SGD build: 10y SGS ~2.4%, ERP 5.5%, through-cycle airline levered beta ~1.3 -> cost of equity ~9.6%; pre-tax cost of debt ~3.5% (notes payable/bank loans, finance-charge note 7) -> ~2.9% after 17% tax; target D/(D+E) ~20% at market (borrowings 7.7bn vs ~20.9bn market cap) -> WACC ~8.3%, rounded to 8.5%. Cyclicality is charged ONCE: the systematic part through the airline beta, the fuel/yield cycle in the scenario flows (FY27 fuel-shock trough in every scenario, a deeper one in bear). No ad-hoc premium, same WACC in every scenario. Terminal cap 12x (cyclical) rather than 20x.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Full lease cash cost = principal 589.1 (C6L.SI_Annual_FY2026.txt:6859) + lease interest 130.3 (note 7) = 719.4 = 3.5% of revenue, charged via lease_cost_pct_path inside EBIT. Lease liabilities (2,978.0) EXCLUDED from net debt; total_debt is borrowings only (5,710.2 non-current + 1,956.5 current = 7,666.7). D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation: total D&A 2,541.4 (depreciation 2,465.6 + amortisation 75.8) less ROU depreciation 494.0 (note 21) = 2,047.4 = 10.0% of revenue, so the lease is not charged twice. Lease cost glides down to 3.0% as SIA's fleet mix shifts to owned aircraft (lease book shrinking 3.8bn->3.0bn over two years), with the matching owned-aircraft cost carried in capex.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (include SIA Engineering at 100%). NCI charged once in the equity bridge at MARKET value: SIAEC (S59.SI) last 2.92 x ~1,123m shares x ~22.3% minority ~= 730; book NCI is 424.3. No NCI leakage in the flows.
inputs.net_cash_composition: Cash and bank balances 7,931.2 + current investments 578.3 + USD fixed deposits 1,689.8 (note 31; held as a capex currency hedge but liquid deposits, reclassified from long-term) = 10,199.3, less borrowings 7,666.7 = net cash 2,532.6 at 31 March 2026. Restricted cash (22.3) excluded.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route) with the non-US/cyclical adaptations -- SIA is a capital-intensive operating airline group, not a financial, REIT or holdco; route = 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'. Through-cycle framing: the FY2021-22 COVID trough and the FY2023-24 yield supercycle are both excluded from the driver anchors; mid-cycle EBITDA (IFRS16, pre-lease) margin of ~21.5% is set between the pre-COVID EBITDAR level (~19-22%) and the post-COVID 24-27% peak. Extreme cyclicality: operating profit ranged from -609.7 (FY22) / ~-4.3bn net loss (FY21) to +2,727.5 (FY24), far beyond a 3x peak-to-trough EBITDA range. FY0 owner FCF 2,446.4 = reported FCF 2,474.5 (OCF 5,103.0 - capex 2,628.5) - SBC 28.1; interest income is NOT deducted because SIA's OCF starts from PBT and strips interest income (289.4) and finance charges, so neither sits in reported FCF. Note FY26 reported FCF is flattered by lease payments sitting in financing (719.4) -- on the treatment-(B) basis FY0 owner FCF is ~1,727. Cash tax: SIA pays almost no cash tax (10.8 paid on a 423.4 provision in FY26; deferred tax liability 2,452) because aircraft capital allowances defer it; the path ramps 6% -> 12% (bear 15%), below the 17% statutory rate because continued fleet growth keeps a structural deferral. Buybacks are only treasury purchases for share plans (32.7), so the flat count is funded. SBC is tiny (0.14% of revenue), so the house/street band nearly collapses. Equity bridge adds associates and JVs at book (Air India at its post-impairment carrying value 1,134.6) because associate profits/losses are excluded from the flows. Air India has sought fresh capital from shareholders -- a future SIA cash call is NOT modelled and is a key downside risk. FY2027 guidance: no numeric guidance; the FY26 AR outlook says jet fuel has more than doubled since the Middle East conflict began, the full impact feeds through in FY2026/27, and fare increases do not fully offset it -- every scenario therefore has an FY27 margin trough. No Q1 FY2027 filing is in the corpus; the latest balance sheet is 31 March 2026.

bear.narrative: Sustained high fuel plus a fuel-driven macro slowdown: FY27 EBITDA falls to 15% and FY28 revenue contracts as premium long-haul demand weakens; Gulf super-connectors and Asian LCCs compress yields back to pre-COVID levels, so mid-cycle margin settles at 19.5% (pre-COVID EBITDAR territory) while committed fleet capex (9.9bn) cannot be cut.

base.narrative: FY27 fuel-shock trough (EBITDA 19% vs 24.1% in FY26) as fare rises lag a doubled jet-fuel price, then recovery to a 21.5% mid-cycle margin by FY29; revenue tracks ~3-4% capacity growth plus fare pass-through; capex 13% of revenue through the 777-9/A350F delivery wave, settling at 11.5% (~1.1x ex-ROU D&A).

bull.narrative: Fuel spike proves short-lived and hedging gains (derivative assets 1,058 at March 2026) cushion FY27; Gulf and Asian competitors retrench capacity under fuel and Middle East disruption, so SIA's premium Changi hub keeps yields near the post-COVID level and margin holds ~23.5%, below the FY23-24 peak but above pre-COVID.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: a fuel shock is already in progress (AR outlook: jet fuel more than doubled, full impact in FY2026/27) and airline earnings are extremely cyclical. Base 50%: the balance sheet (net cash 2.5bn ex-leases) removes solvency risk, so the downside is margin, not survival. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs both a quick fuel retreat and yields staying well above pre-COVID against rising Gulf/LCC capacity -- two independent things going right.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
